name: Bright Boost
description: The tight boost with the tone well up: some 3 dB more from 700 Hz upward, for a dark guitar or an amplifier with the treble held back. Put it before the amplifier.

name: Dark and Thick
description: The drive past its middle and the tone all the way down: the hump moves down to 530 Hz and 5 dB comes off between 1.5 and 3 kHz, for a smooth, woolly overdrive under a voice.

name: Full Drive
description: The drive at its top and the tone just under its middle: as much as the pedal clips, 28 dB up at 800 Hz on a quiet signal and held to a diode's drop on a loud one.

name: Gentle Push
description: The drive off and the level at three quarters: 12 dB in the middle and nothing at 80 Hz, enough to tip an amplifier on the edge of breaking up over it when the strings are hit.

name: Low Crunch
description: The drive a third up: chords that are nearly clean played softly and gritty when dug into, with the lows left clean under them.

name: Noon
description: The drive and the tone at their middle: the pedal's own overdrive, soft clipping with the middle 18 dB up and the top rolled off above it.

name: Singing Lead
description: The drive well up and the tone a little past its middle, for single notes: a note played softly comes out nearly as loud as one played hard, and cuts through in the middle.

name: Tight Boost
description: The drive nearly off and the level at its top, as the pedal is used before a high-gain amplifier: 16 dB more at 800 Hz and under 4 at 80, so the amplifier is driven harder in the middle and hardly harder in the lows, which tightens muted rhythm playing. Put it before the amplifier.
